findings.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous and omits group/resource
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates namespace, user UID, action, name and parent folder with '_' separators. Since resource/folder UIDs may legally contain underscores, two different (name, parent) pairs can produce the identical key (e.g. name="a_b", parent="c" vs name="a", parent="b_c"), causing a denial cached for one resource to be returned for a different one. The key also does not include group/resource, so two different group/resource pairs that map to the same action string would share denial entries. The consequence is incorrect (false) denials for up to the cache TTL. Include a non-ambiguous separator/encoding (e.g. length-prefixed or escaped segments) and the group/resource in the key.

findings.title: Error from getCachedIdentityPermissions silently swallowed
findings.body: In Check, the error from getCachedIdentityPermissions is only compared against nil; real errors (e.g. GetUserIdentifiers DB failure or 'unsupported identity type') are indistinguishable from cache.ErrNotFound and are neither logged nor traced. This hides genuine failures and makes debugging cache/identity-store problems hard. Distinguish cache.ErrNotFound from other errors and log/return the latter.

findings.title: permissionCacheUsage metric counted twice for a single Check
findings.body: When cached permissions are found but do not grant access, the code increments permissionCacheUsage with label "false" at line 137 after having consulted the cache successfully; conversely a denial-cache hit at line 118 increments "true" and then returns. The 'false' bucket therefore counts cache hits that simply didn't grant permission, so the cache hit-rate metric no longer reflects actual cache hits and will look much worse than reality.

findings.title: Denial-cache test does not prove the permission cache is bypassed
findings.body: The comment says "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked" but the permCache entry is set to map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}, i.e. a deny, so the assertion assert.False(resp.Allowed) would pass even if the denial cache were not consulted at all. Set the value to true (an allow) so the test actually verifies that the denial cache short-circuits before the permission cache.
